_meta.indication: EBANGA is indicated for the treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus in adult and pediatric patients, including neonates born to a mother who is RT-PCR positive for Zaire ebolavirus infection

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial (control: ZMapp) conducted during the 2018 Zaire ebolavirus outbreak in the DRC
pivotal_trials.population: Persons with confirmed EBOV (Zaire ebolavirus) infection at a participating Ebola Treatment Unit; adults and children
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was the 28-day mortality rate
pivotal_trials.n: 681 subjects randomized overall; primary analysis in concurrent ITT population comparing ansuvimab-zykl (N=174) vs ZMapp (N=168)
pivotal_trials.result: 28-day mortality 35.1% (61/174) with ansuvimab-zykl vs 49.4% (83/168) with ZMapp; rate difference -14.4% (95% CI -24.8, -2.4); Boschloo's two-sided p=0.0075

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse events (>=5%) were pyrexia, tachycardia, diarrhea, vomiting, hypotension, tachypnea, and chills; in the trial pyrexia 17% (vs 58% control), tachycardia 9% (vs 32%), hypotension 8% (vs 31%), chills 5% (vs 33%). Key safety concern is hypersensitivity reactions including infusion-associated events, which may be acute and life-threatening.
target_moa: Ansuvimab-zykl is a recombinant fully human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that targets the Zaire ebolavirus glycoprotein (glycan cap and core domains of the GP1 subunit), preventing EBOV entry into cells and inhibiting the virus

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not taken to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues and there were no controversial issues

basis.text: Ansuvimab-zykl received Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of Zaire ebolavirus infection

citations.quote: The regulatory history is notable for Orphan Drug designation and Breakthrough Therapy designation. This BLA received a Priority Review and was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, because ansuvimab-zykl received Breakthrough Therapy designation, and the benefit-risk assessment was not controversial based on the review team's preliminary assessment of the trial results.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation (#2019-6830) granted May 8, 2019 for the treatment of patients with EBOV infection

This BLA received a Priority Review and was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, because ansuvimab-zykl received Breakthrough Therapy designation

summary.text: Ansuvimab-zykl received Orphan Drug designation (May 8, 2019) and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and the BLA received Priority Review; the application was not taken to an advisory committee. Approval was based on the single Phase 2/3 randomized controlled PALM Trial, which showed a significant reduction in 28-day mortality versus control.

citations.quote: The regulatory history is notable for Orphan Drug designation and Breakthrough Therapy designation. This BLA received a Priority Review and was not presented at the Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee, because ansuvimab-zykl received Breakthrough Therapy designation, and the benefit-risk assessment was not controversial based on the review team's preliminary assessment of the trial results.

The results of the PALM Trial clearly demonstrated efficacy to support the approval of ansuvimab-zykl for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients infected with EBOV. The PALM Trial was stopped early on the basis of a prespecified interim analysis and showed a significant reduction in mortality for ansuvimab-zykl (35%) compared to control (49%). The results from this single trial are adequate

requirement.text: 3965-1: Identify all amino acid polymorphisms in the ansuvimab-zykl epitope (GP positions 111-119) and amino acids within 5 Angstroms from available EBOV GP sequences and perform phenotypic assessments of the impact on neutralization, including EBOV GP substitutions L111I and L111F

citations.quote: 3965-1 Conduct a study to identify all amino acid polymorphisms in the ansuvimab-zykl epitope (GP positions 111-119) and amino acids within 5 Angstroms from currently available *Zaire ebolavirus* (EBOV) GP sequences in public databases and perform phenotypic assessments to determine the impact that each of the substitutions have on ansuvimab-zykl neutralization using lentivirus-based particles pseudotyped with EBOV GP containing each of the substitutions. Also include EBOV GP substitutions L111I and L111F in your phenotypic analyses.

requirement.text: 3965-2: Identify ansuvimab-zykl resistance pathways using a recombinant virus expressing EBOV glycoprotein to select and characterize several independent resistant isolates phenotypically and genotypically

citations.quote: 3965-2 Conduct a study to identify *ansuvimab-zykl* resistance pathways using a recombinant virus expressing *Zaire ebolavirus* (EBOV) glycoprotein (GP) to select and characterize several independent resistant isolates phenotypically and genotypically.

requirement.text: 3965-3: Submit all sequencing data for patients treated with ansuvimab-zykl in the PALM and MEURI trials and perform resistance analyses with a study report

citations.quote: 3965-3 Submit all sequencing data that become available for patients who were treated with ansuvimab-zykl in the PALM and MEURI trials. Perform resistance analyses of these sequences and provide a study report discussing the approaches used and the resistance results generated.

requirement.text: 3965-4: Design and conduct a trial evaluating efficacy, safety and PK of a higher dose of Ebanga vs Ebanga 50 mg/kg in EBOV-infected patients with cycle-threshold values <=22 to determine whether a change in dosing regimen is needed

citations.quote: 3965-4 Collaborate with US public health agencies, other public health agencies and local health authorities, as appropriate to design and conduct a trial to evaluate the efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetics of a higher dose of Ebanga (ansuvimab-zykl) vs. Ebanga (ansuvimab-zykl) 50 mg/kg in *Zaire ebolavirus* infected adult and pediatric patients with cycle-threshold (CT) values for nucleoprotein gene targets of less than or equal to 22 to determine if a change in dosing regimen is needed in these patients.
